method: Whitespace word counts. Full title/date/summary/notes are charged to all cited pages by default, with field-level exceptions only for date-only corroboration, specific clauses, and original editorial qualifications. Chapter introductions are also included. No lyrics or verbatim source quotations appear. Creative sonic cues, navigation labels and schema descriptions are original design directions, not source summaries.

attribution_details.counted_text: Pink Floyd takes shape 1965 London brings Syd Barrett, Roger Waters, Richard Wright and Nick Mason into the group that becomes Pink Floyd. Barrett supplies a name drawn from blues musicians Pink Anderson and Floyd Council. Cambridge friendships and the London student music scene form the foundations of a band soon moving beyond its rhythm-and-blues beginnings.

attribution_details.counted_text: A home in the London underground 1966 Pink Floyd develops its improvisational identity amid London’s underground scene, playing the Marquee’s Spontaneous Underground, London Free School events and the emerging UFO club. Extended music and projected light become parts of one experience. These small rooms establish an approach to performance that later expands into much larger spaces.

attribution_details.counted_text: Arnold Layne reaches the record shops 1967-03-10 The UK release of Arnold Layne introduces Syd Barrett’s songwriting to listeners. Recorded at Sound Techniques, it takes Pink Floyd beyond its underground following. The band balances concise pop records with the extended improvisations that distinguish its concerts and identity. Date is the UK single release.

attribution_details.counted_text: Games for May puts sound in motion 1967-05-12 At London’s Queen Elizabeth Hall, Games for May places Pink Floyd in a concert-hall setting with a deliberately theatrical presentation. The Azimuth Co-ordinator allows sound to move around the room. The show makes spatial audio and the audience’s physical surroundings central parts of the band’s developing visual and musical language.

attribution_details.counted_text: See Emily Play becomes a UK hit 1967-06-16 See Emily Play is released and reaches number six on the UK singles chart. Barrett’s compact, imaginative pop songwriting brings the group to a wider audience, including television. The single offers another entrance into a band whose stage performances can already stretch far beyond the three-minute format. Date is the UK single release, not the date of its chart peak.

attribution_details.counted_text: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn 1967-08-04 Pink Floyd’s debut combines Barrett’s concise, eccentric songs with the exploratory spirit of the band’s live improvisations. Recorded with producer Norman Smith, it is the only album to feature Barrett throughout. Its title comes from The Wind in the Willows, placing a literary pastoral image beside the group’s electric experimentation. UK release: 4 August 1967. The official chronology dates the differently configured US edition to 21 October 1967.

attribution_details.counted_text: Five musicians, then a new quartet 1968-01 David Gilmour joins Pink Floyd, briefly creating a five-piece band with Barrett, Waters, Wright and Mason. The official chronology records the five-piece debut at Aston University on 12 January and a Southampton performance without Barrett on 26 January. The transition changes both the stage lineup and the band’s songwriting balance. This card covers the January performing transition. Barrett’s formal separation and management changes unfolded over the following months; it is not a claim that he formally left on 26 January.

attribution_details.counted_text: A Saucerful of Secrets 1968-06-28 The second album captures the change from Barrett’s band to the Gilmour, Waters, Wright and Mason quartet. Recordings from both periods sit together, including Barrett’s Jugband Blues. The title piece develops a larger structural approach, while Hipgnosis begins the album-cover relationship that becomes inseparable from Pink Floyd’s visual identity. Date is the UK release. Barrett appears on three tracks according to the official album guide.

attribution_details.counted_text: Live music for the moon landing 1969-07-20 Pink Floyd supplies live music for the BBC’s television coverage surrounding the first Moon landing. The performance known as Moonhead connects the band’s atmospheric improvisation to an event unfolding in real time. It is a distinctive meeting of experimental rock, broadcasting and the imagery of the space age. The official chronology dates the appearance to 20 July; the BBC coverage extended across the night.

attribution_details.counted_text: Ummagumma 1969-11-07 Ummagumma divides a double album between live performances and separate studio contributions from each of the four musicians. Concert pieces show the group’s collective power, while the studio record exposes contrasting individual interests. Its hybrid format makes it an unusual entry in the standard sequence of fifteen Pink Floyd studio albums. The official chronology dates the UK release to 7 November and the US release to 8 November 1969. This is a live/studio hybrid, counted once in the standard fifteen-album sequence.

attribution_details.counted_text: Performing inside an empty amphitheatre 1971-10-04 Filming begins in the ancient amphitheatre at Pompeii under director Adrian Maben. Pink Floyd performs without a conventional concert audience, letting the musicians, equipment and surrounding ruins carry the images. The encounter between a contemporary electric band and an ancient site becomes one of its defining audiovisual documents. Four days of location filming began on 4 October 1971; additional filming took place later in Paris. The film’s premiere belongs to 1972.

attribution_details.counted_text: The circular screen enters the show 1974-06 The French tour introduces Pink Floyd’s circular projection screen, giving films and images a strong architectural place above the musicians. New material also appears onstage, including Shine On You Crazy Diamond and Raving and Drooling. During the year, touring becomes a workshop for music that will feed more than one future album. UK release: 12 September 1975; the official chronology gives 13 September for the US. No precise date is assigned here to Barrett’s unannounced studio visit.

attribution_details.counted_text: A pig above Battersea 1976-12-02 The Animals cover shoot places an inflatable pig above Battersea Power Station.
